### How this work is cited

Passages inside Liji (Book of Rites) are identified by chapter by name. A compilation of ritual texts rather than an authored book. Two of its chapters — the Zhongyong and the Daxue — were removed from it by Zhu Xi and made independent canonical works, which is why the corpus cites them both as 'Liji, <chapter>' and under their own titles.

### The work in The Great Learning’s thought

The Dàxué is the shortest of the Four Books and the most programmatic. Like the Zhōngyōng it was lifted out of the Lǐjì by Zhu Xi, and it is traditionally divided into a brief 'classic' section attributed to Confucius and a commentary attributed to his disciple Zengzi. [More on The Great Learning](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-great-learning) .
